alt: Four panels of features. Group rapport: in-group lexis, inclusive pronouns, shared references, back-channelling. Power and status: conversational control, forms of address, imperatives and modals, specialist lexis. Identity and relationship: self-presentation, politeness, register and variety, phatic talk. Play: wordplay, banter, performance, shared routines.
caption: Each credited area has its own features; the same feature can serve more than one area.

alt: Four paired concepts: Giles’s converging and diverging; Wareing’s instrumental and influential power; Fairclough’s power in discourse and power behind discourse; Brown and Levinson’s positive and negative face. Below, communities of practice: groups formed around a shared activity develop shared ways of speaking.
caption: Each framework gives a pair of terms; apply them to a specific moment, not in the abstract.

alt: Three columns. Spoken texts: turn-taking, interruption and overlap, adjacency pairs, back-channelling, prosody, with non-fluency treated as normal. Written texts: forms of address, pronouns, register, modality, structure. Multimodal texts: how image, layout, typography and words combine, such as a club post using emoji, hashtags and group photos.
caption: Section A texts can be spoken, written or multimodal; each mode has its own features to analyse.

alt: The debating-team transcript with annotations: Priya’s discourse markers, imperative and interruption assert power; Tom’s hedges attend to her negative face; “yes boss” and “the Supreme Leader has spoken” are mock deference that builds rapport; her final question accommodates the group’s challenge.
caption: Power, politeness and banter overlap in the same exchange: the captain’s power is negotiated.

alt: The gaming community post beside a screenshot of celebrating avatars, annotated: “GG”, “raid”, “boss” and “mods” are in-group lexis marking membership; “Our squad” builds rapport; the moderators’ nap joke is playful self-deprecation softening their status; the image shows the shared success.
caption: In a multimodal text, analyse how the image and the words work together.

alt: Five steps: establish the context; scan for each credited area; select four or five rich moments; name, quote and explain using at least two frameworks; and note observations that could feed the Section B essay.
caption: Context, scan, select, analyse, and bank evidence for the Section B essay.
